notes: DOCUMENTED TARGET - NOT RECORDABLE (daemon_capability: incapable). This spec states the arc the row asserts so a future re-assessment has something concrete to compare against; it is NOT expected to pass on mistral-vibe as it stands, and it is deliberately NOT weakened to match what the daemon can see. THE ROW: two DISTINCT waiting episodes in one session - one raised by a MUTATING tool, one by a READ-ONLY tool - arc ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready, with a final ready surviving a >=10s trailing idle. AGENT LAYER (satisfied): vibe 2.19.1 gates read-only tools by their own declaration, not just mutating ones. web_fetch (builtins/web_fetch.py:63) and web_search (:50) declare ToolPermission.ASK; web_fetch's resolve_permission returns ASK with a per-domain URL_PATTERN RequiredPermission (:94-113). read_file declares ALWAYS (read_file.py:78) but routes through resolve_file_tool_permission (core/tools/utils.py:64-124), which returns ASK whenever the path matches sensitive_patterns (default **/.env) or fails is_path_within_workdir - an OUTSIDE_DIRECTORY escalation. Mutating side: write_file ASK (:40), edit ASK (:67), bash ASK (:259). So two gates from two DIFFERENT tools are raisable on stock config. TRANSPORT LAYER (why this cannot pass): nothing whatsoever reaches the watched messages.jsonl while an approval prompt is held - not the tool result, and not even the assistant tool_calls line that raised it. SessionLogger.save_interaction (core/session/session_logger.py:306) is the only writer, and _conversation_loop (_loop.py:1144) calls _save_messages() only AFTER _perform_llm_turn() returns (:1195-1197, the code's own comment: 'Per-turn save ... after the inner loop'), while _perform_llm_turn (:1319) runs _handle_tool_calls - which blocks in _ask_approval (:1734) - to completion first. _open_user_turn (:1108) saves nothing either. The daemon therefore sees a silent write-gap and classifies working throughout. The one hook irrlicht installs for vibe is post_agent_turn (vibe/hooks.go), which fires at TURN END; before_tool - the only event that fires at the right moment, and which does carry tool_name + tool_call_id (vibe/core/hooks/models.py BeforeToolInvocation) - is deliberately not installed, because it fires before vibe's own permission check (_loop.py:1533 before :1547) and cannot say whether a given call will prompt. Consequently ALL FOUR waiting rules are dead here: permission_prompt (hook-tier, no such hook), transcript_permission_prompt (needs ParsedEvent.PermissionRequestIDs, which vibe/parser.go never sets), user_blocking_tool (ask_user_question/exit_plan_mode only - scenarios 2.17/2.18), and open_tool_stalled (needs HasOpenToolCall, which is never true during a vibe gate because the tool_calls line and its result land in the same post-approval append). NOTE THAT VIBE IS NOT AN INSTANCE OF #1861's DEFECT SHAPE: there is no per-tool-name allowlist here for a read-only tool to fall out of. Its read-only gates are invisible for exactly the same transport reason its mutating gates are, so a future green here would prove the transport changed, not that tool-class parity was fixed. WHAT THE PHASES BELOW DO NOT EXPRESS - the vacuous-pass trap for this row: the phase schema carries NO tool-name field, so nothing here can bind mutating_gate and readonly_gate to two DIFFERENT tools, and that binding is the whole row. If this cell is ever unfrozen, a recipe driving two `bash` calls (one `cat`, one `echo >`) makes every phase green while testing nothing about tool class, because bash is ASK and both halves would gate identically. The verify must assert out of band that the recording's messages.jsonl carries two assistant tool_calls with two DIFFERENT function.name values (e.g. write_file and read_file). The phase ORDER (mutating first) is arbitrary and is NOT part of the row's claim - the scenario says so explicitly. A SECOND LOAD-BEARING PRECONDITION for any future recording: each dialog must be answered with the ONE-TIME option, never 'always'. An 'always' answer adds an ApprovedRule to the session PermissionStore (core/tools/permissions.py PermissionStore.add_rule/covers), after which _should_execute_tool's `if ctx.required_permissions and not uncovered` branch executes silently and the second gate never opens. And vibe must be launched WITHOUT --auto-approve/--yolo: bypass_tool_permissions short-circuits _should_execute_tool (:1690) before any prompt. ANCHORING follows this column's confirmed presession shape (see 2-1 basic-turn's backflow note): a transient proc-<PID> row is born ready before the lazily-created transcript dir appears, then reconciles into the real session_<id> under a DIFFERENT session_id, so the birth is two phases and every later phase chains through same_session_as: session_birth. OBSERVATIONS assert agent only. mistral-vibe's model and tokens come from the meta.json sidecar, which the offline replay golden cannot reproduce (replay stages only transcript.jsonl), so cost_nonzero/tokens_nonzero are false on this whole column - and a model pin on a cell that is never recorded would be a doc-guess.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready within 1s of launch (the CommandPattern scanner binds the vibe PID before the transcript dir exists). It never goes working; it exists only so the real birth below is not mis-anchored to it.
The real session_<id> reconciles with a DISTINCT session_id when ~/.vibe/logs/session/<id>/ appears, born ready. Every phase below anchors here.
vibe PID bound to the real session (matched by cwd via the meta.json sidecar)
The prompt that needs both a mutating and a read-only tool call drives ready -> working on the real session

MUTATING half: a write_file call (ToolPermission.ASK, builtins/write_file.py:40) opens vibe's Textual approval widget and the session goes working -> waiting while the modal is on screen. This is the half 2.19 already covers; it is here so one recording can compare the two calls. On vibe today NOTHING is written to messages.jsonl at this moment, which is why the cell is frozen.
The user answers the first dialog with the ONE-TIME option (never 'always' - see the meta note) and the session resumes waiting -> working. The episode ends on the ANSWER, not on the turn.

THE PHASE THIS ROW EXISTS FOR. A second, DISTINCT dialog raised by a tool that only READS - read_file of a path outside the workdir (ASK via the OUTSIDE_DIRECTORY escalation, core/tools/utils.py:106-118) or web_fetch (ASK via URL_PATTERN, web_fetch.py:94-113) - produces its OWN waiting episode: not skipped, and not merged into the mutating call's episode. It must come from a DIFFERENT tool than the mutating half; the schema cannot assert that, so the verify must (see the meta note).
The user answers the second dialog (one-time again) and the session resumes waiting -> working

The turn finishes back to ready - full arc ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready. On vibe the only signal that would carry this is the post_agent_turn hook / the terminal assistant message, both of which arrive only after everything above has already been missed.
The session is still ready after a >=10s trailing idle: it does not remain waiting after the last dialog closes, and no late post-tool signal bounces it back
